title: What If Every Sponge in the Ocean Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every sea sponge vanished? Coral reefs would starve, and sponges don't even have a brain.
Reefs are a puzzle. They're packed with life in water almost empty of nutrients.
Corals can release up to half of their organic matter into the sea, where most animals can't use it.
Sponges catch it. Scientists call this the sponge loop, and it turns waste into food within two days.
Sponges recycle about ten times as much matter as bacteria, and their output rivals all the corals and algae combined.
Take them away, and the reef's recycling stops. The richest ecosystem in the sea would run out of fuel.

description:
What if every sea sponge vanished?
Sponges recycle the organic matter that corals release, a system called the sponge loop, which keeps reefs alive in nutrient-poor water.
